mostWorthwhile.text: Gathering the gas was most worthwhile: it connected gravity with the distinction between expanding space and bound regions, while noting that further contraction requires heat loss.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining neutral hydrogen and helium felt comparatively routine; the resulting gas composition was informative, but the choice was the only offered action.

surprise.text: I was struck that bound regions need not expand with the rest of space, and that the universe became transparent before the first stars shone.

arbitrary.text: Combining primordial gas with trapped radiation was a somewhat abstract way to represent light being freed; its purpose was clear, even if the physical interaction was less intuitive.

continue.text: I would continue: the concise explanations of early-universe processes make me curious how the story connects primordial gas to later stars and worlds, although the forced combinations offer limited decisions.
